slides.headline: A clown is dying in the snow. Why?
slides.sub: Jean-Léon Gérôme, The Duel After the Masquerade, 1857

slides.headline: Paris, at dawn
slides.text: A grey winter dawn in the Bois de Boulogne, Paris. A few hours ago, these men were dancing at a masked ball. Then something went wrong.

slides.headline: Pierrot
slides.text: Dressed as Pierrot, the sad clown of the theatre, a man sinks into the snow. He has just lost a sword duel.

slides.headline: The Duke
slides.text: A friend in the costume of the Duc de Guise holds him up. Last night it was a game. Now it is real.

slides.headline: The doge
slides.text: Even the surgeon is still in costume, a Venetian doge, kneeling in the snow, trying to stop the bleeding.

slides.headline: The black domino
slides.text: Behind them, another masked guest in a black domino clutches his head. No one expected the party to end like this.

slides.headline: The winner
slides.text: Meanwhile, on the right, the winner walks away, dressed as an American Indian, his second Harlequin at his side.

slides.headline: Left behind
slides.text: He leaves his sword lying in the snow, with a few feathers from his headdress. He doesn't look back.

slides.headline: No answer
slides.text: Paris was obsessed with it in 1857 and argued about what really happened. Gérôme never said. What do you think started it?
